what_happened: The route command was RIGHT, but after handoff the ego went left across the double-yellow center line. By 7.2s it was driving at about 10.5 m/s in the oncoming lane, about 9 m from the recorded path. It kept going straight on the wrong side of the road and hit oncoming car 85 head-on at 9.2s without braking; the rear contact came after.

After crossing the intersection, the ego stayed too far left, on the line of the parked cars, instead of moving right toward the travel lane like the recorded path. It kept a steady speed of about 4.7 m/s and drove front-first into parked car 68 as the gap closed from 23 m to about 4 m. It never braked or steered around the car.

Wrong-way driving. The ego was about 8.6 m off the recorded path and driving left of the yellow center line, in the oncoming lanes. It kept speeding up (10 to 11.5 m/s) while oncoming traffic came toward it: it passed oncoming vehicle 85, then hit the oncoming white van (actor 86) on its front-left at 11.2 s. The gap to the van dropped from 32 m to 4.6 m in one second, which only happens head-on.

After handoff the ego kept going at about 13 m/s and drifted about 2 m left of the recorded path, toward the parked cars along the left curb. Its planned path called for a right turn. The ego barely slowed (13.6 to 12.3 m/s) while the gap to parked car 6 ahead closed from 35 m to 4 m, and its front-left hit that car.

The route said RIGHT and the recorded path moved right across the lanes. The ego instead stayed in the leftmost lane at about 7–8 m/s, then steered left into the landscaped median at the U-turn opening and left the road at 10.3 s, 6.2 m from the recorded path. The camera view was clean before the drift.

The route said turn RIGHT, but after handoff the ego went the other way. It moved left across the lanes toward the left side of the road and ended up on the grass median just before the intersection at 8.8 s, 6.4 m off the recorded path. No collision is visible in the frames, and the camera view was clean before the drift started, so the policy's path choice caused this.

The command was RIGHT and the route turned right, but at the intersection the ego turned left at about 3.6 m/s. Its front then hit vehicle 155, a white car near the corner of the left-hand street, about 5.8 m off the recorded path. The later rear contact came after this front collision.

While turning right at low speed (about 3 m/s) into a narrow street lined with parked cars, the ego took the turn too tight. Its front ran into parked car 80 (the red car on the right in the camera view), about 7.5 m off the recorded human path.

After handoff the ego kept going at about 12–14 m/s but drifted left out of its lane toward the row of parked cars along the left curb, even though the command had changed to RIGHT. It hit parked car 6 with its front at 6.9 s: the gap closed from 35 m to 3.9 m with almost no braking, and the ego was flagged offroad about 2.1 m from where the human drove.

After handoff the ego was about 7–9 m left of the recorded path, driving in the oncoming lane while the command was RIGHT. It kept speeding up (10→12 m/s) and hit oncoming van 86 head-on at 11.2 s. The van had its headlights on in the 10.2 s camera frame, and the gap closed at about 28 m/s, so it was coming toward the ego.

The route command was RIGHT and the planned path ran to the right lanes. Instead, the ego held about 8 m/s and drifted steadily left across its lane toward the median until it ran onto the grassy, tree-lined median at 9.9 s, 6.2 m from the human's recorded path. The camera view looked clean before the departure, and no actor was involved.

The route command was RIGHT and the recorded path went ahead and to the right through the intersection, but the ego turned left at about 3.5 m/s. It cut the corner into the side street and its front hit vehicle 155, which sat near the curb at the street's entrance.

After handoff at 4.7 s the ego went straight at about 9.5 m/s, but its plan (orange) bent left, out of its lane. It drifted left into vehicle 33, which was driving alongside in the adjacent left lane, and hit it at 6.4 s. The route command had just switched to RIGHT, and the vehicle ahead was still about 17 m away, so the ego did not need to move over.

The route command was RIGHT and the recorded path went across the intersection, but the ego turned left into the side street at about 3.5 m/s. It drove its front into vehicle 155, which was in that street's lane; the gap shrank from 9.0 m to 4.6 m without the ego braking. When it hit, the ego was about 6 m off the recorded path. A rear contact was also recorded, but the front collision came first.

On a narrow residential street, with the route asking for a right turn ahead, the ego kept going at about 13 m/s and drifted left toward the cars parked along the left curb. It ran front-first into parked car 6, slowing only slightly as the gap shrank from 35 m to 4 m. The camera view was clear beforehand, and the rear contact flagged in the input is not what caused the failure.

The route said RIGHT, but the ego drifted left across the double-yellow centre line into the oncoming lane at about 10 m/s, ending 8.3 m from the human's path. It hit oncoming car 85 nearly head-on: the gap closed from 17 m to 3 m in half a second and the ego never braked.

The policy took over at 4.7 s, going straight at about 9.7 m/s. It then planned a path (orange) that veered left out of its lane toward the lane of actor 33, which was driving alongside on its left. By 6.3 s the ego had moved left into actor 33 and caused a side collision, though the lead car was still about 17 m ahead and the green recorded path stayed straight.

The route command was RIGHT and the planned route went to the right, but the policy held about 8 m/s and drifted left across the leftmost lane onto the palm-tree median, where it went offroad 6.1 m from the recorded path. The camera view was clean before the drift, so a broken render doesn't explain it.

The ego was making the commanded right turn at about 3–4 m/s and cut it much tighter than the human driver did. It ended up in the curbside parking lane of the cross street, about 7 m off the recorded path, and drove front-first into parked car 90. The camera view smeared once the ego was that far off the recorded path, but the ego had already started the too-tight turn at 10 s.

After handoff, the ego sped up from 8.6 to 9.5 m/s and held a straight heading while the road bent right, even after the command changed to RIGHT. It drifted left into the parking lane and its front hit parked car 31 on the left edge of the road, about 1.6 m from the recorded human path.

After crossing the intersection at about 4.5 m/s, the ego drifted toward the left side of the street and drove front-first into parked car 68, a dark Audi at the left curb. It never braked or steered away, and the gap closed from 11 m to 4 m. The planned path and the recorded route both stayed in the middle of the lane, so this was a drift into a parked car, not a vehicle ahead in its lane, and the later rear contact is secondary.

The ego was approaching the intersection at about 4.5 m/s on a route that turns right. After handoff its plan (orange) bent left and straight across the junction instead of following the right turn, and the ego started yawing left. It was flagged offroad at 6.0 s, near the stop line, with no collision and no lead vehicle close by (the gap ahead was over 30 m).

Although the route command was RIGHT, the ego had drifted left across the double-yellow centerline and was driving in the opposing lane, about 9 m from the recorded path. It hit an oncoming white van (actor 86) head-on at about 12 m/s. The gap closed at roughly 28 m/s, faster than the ego's own speed, so the van was coming toward it, and the ego never braked.

After the policy took over at 4.7 s, the ego left its lane while going straight at about 9.5 m/s. Its plan bent left, away from the recorded path, toward the left-hand lane. Vehicle 33 was driving alongside in that lane, and the ego's side hit it at 6.3 s, roughly 1.1 m off the recorded path.

The route command was STRAIGHT and then RIGHT at the intersection, but after handoff at 4.7 s the policy's planned path (orange) went straight and then left. The ego drifted left out of its right-turn lane near the stop line, at about 4.5–4.8 m/s, and was flagged offroad at 6.0 s. It was only about 0.5 m from the human trajectory then, so the offroad call is marginal, but the policy was clearly not following the route.

The ego was approaching a signalized intersection at about 4.4 m/s, and its route turned right. After handoff, the policy's planned path drifted slightly left of the route and then bent further left across the intersection, ignoring the right turn. At 6.0 s the ego was flagged offroad near the stop line, where the lanes split, while only 0.5 m from the human's recorded path. So it is a marginal boundary clip, not a clear departure from the road.

After handoff, the policy's planned path (orange) veered left out of the ego's lane at about 8 m/s, while the recorded human path went straight. The ego cut into the adjacent left lane and its front hit actor 33, which was driving alongside it, at 6.2 s.

The route said turn RIGHT, and the recorded path ran several lanes to the right. Instead, the ego stayed in a left lane and drifted further left as it slowed into the intersection. At 8.9 s it ran up onto the left median island by the crosswalk (offroad goes to 1, 6.1 m from the recorded path), and the collision metrics stay at 0.
